purpose: Twenty existing individually findable reading routes with scoped source paths and actual credited pictures. Overlapping people names are not counted as distinct nations.

profiles.name: Lenape
profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: Texas migration, diplomacy, family histories and removal need directly inspected original records and fuller community-authored scholarship. An encyclopedia account is not a completed Texas foundation.
The 1859 Brazos-reserve relocation and an around-1873 Wichita-allotment narrative describe potentially different stages or scopes; resolve original records before a single detailed chronology.

Current governments, homeland communities, citizenship and recognition require individually scoped contemporary evidence. One publisher’s position in identity disputes is not an Atlas-wide adjudication.
Moraviantown’s battle-outcome description and universal first-treaty assertion are not adopted. Undated population, land figures and legal claims are omitted.
Munsee and other language varieties, Canadian community histories, women’s histories, later land/government changes and wider Lenape-authored work remain unevenly covered.
Original archival records, treaty implementation, current legal instruments and books cited by the institutional histories remain unread. The scholarly article is a selected-page inspection.
No ceremonial narratives, sensitive places, songs, restricted records, current speaker totals or automatic descent/affiliation claims are reproduced.
No researched-count or adequacy change is proposed for Delaware (Lenape) original97; its original bibliography and reciprocal reading route must remain.

profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: More Nimiipuu-authored histories, language publications and distinct Colville, Umatilla and Idaho community perspectives remain to be reviewed.
The nonprofit's account is organizational self-description; independent program evaluation, original oral recordings and long-term restoration outcomes were not examined.
Original treaty scans, oral interpretations, band-specific narratives and the linked 1877 material remain unread. No present treaty-rights or homeland-boundary conclusion is proposed.
No Nimiipuu community review or endorsement is recorded. The Spalding photograph depicts a public NPS visitor center, not a tribal government building or all Nimiipuu community life.

profiles.name: Northern Paiute
profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: This selection combines linguistic orientation with one joint government's history; other Northern Paiute community histories, authors, foodways, education and present language work remain uneven.
The 2020 editors' introduction was inspected in selected sections; individual contributed narratives and the complete volume were not reviewed.
Duck Valley is a Western Shoshone–Northern Paiute joint government and one local history. Bannock linguistic classification does not erase distinct Bannock community or governmental identities.

Original executive orders, constitutions and later amendments were not added in this bounded selection. No current population, present legal-status audit, boundary or membership conclusion is proposed.

The 2026-10-23/24 review dates and scopes come from the saved reviewed draft, not a new full-source review. Berkeley and Duck Valley public bodies were additionally opened for current visual/context checks on October 27, without changing those retained review dates.
No Northern Paiute community review or endorsement is recorded. The photo concerns a specifically identified Duck Valley project in 2015.

profiles.name: Paiute
profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: Paiute is a broad route through distinct Northern and Southern usages, not a single people, government, language or territory. Additional individual nations need their own community sources.
The Northern Paiute language account does not supply a full Southern Paiute linguistic comparison; Southern Paiute and Chemehuevi community-authored language scholarship remain to be reviewed.

Duck Valley and San Juan Southern Paiute are different, specifically scoped examples. Neither supplies a universal Paiute history, and a joint Shoshone-Paiute project should not be presented as exclusively Paiute.
The San Juan account's current land/treaty status, original documents and outcomes were not evaluated. No current legal, acreage, demographic or membership claim is made.

Northern Paiute language/Duck Valley evidence retains actual October 24/23 review dates from the saved draft; it is reused evidence, not newly read global scholarship. No community review or endorsement is recorded.

profiles.name: Dakota
profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: The Upper Sioux Community government website returned HTTP 403 to this research request. The accessible state-hosted histories and 2025 government guide provide useful community-attributed material, but the current Community constitution, official land-conveyance instrument, and a direct government publication about the 2024 return remain unreviewed; the access failure is not treated as a paywall and was not bypassed.

Dakota communities outside Minnesota, including particular governments in the Dakotas, Nebraska, and Canada, need their own community voices and scoped sources. This collection is not an exhaustive homeland or present-community map.
Specialist Dakota language scholarship is needed for precise language variation and classification; undated public speaker totals should not be used as current demographic findings.

Original treaty scans, oral understandings, 1863 statutes, community constitutions, and additional Dakota-authored historical scholarship would deepen the collection. Treaty text, state summaries, and public exhibition testimony answer different questions.

The complete Mni Sóta Maḳoce lesson materials require teacher training; the public page gives the curriculum overview but not the lessons themselves. Outcome research was described by the publisher as forthcoming, so no effectiveness claim is made.

Dated education reports and community evaluations would be needed before describing current operations, participation, or outcomes. No clinical, legal, membership, or service-eligibility conclusion is proposed.
No Dakota community review or endorsement is recorded.

profiles.name: Santee Dakota
profiles.regionalPriority: Texas, Idaho, Minnesota, Blackfoot and Great Lakes communities
remainingGaps: This is a wider Santee/Eastern Dakota route. Additional Wahpeton, Sisseton, Wahpekute and Mdewakanton communities, including Canadian perspectives, remain underrepresented.

The college's historical synthesis and the Flandreau/Lower Sioux institutional accounts answer different questions. They are not evidence that every Santee person followed the same displacement route or belonged to one government.
Original treaty/agency records, community-authored scholarship, distinct Dakota language work and public testimony beyond these selected accounts remain unread.

The reused Lower Sioux source retains its October 21 actual-review date and exact source object. Its photo-context page was reopened October 27 for site identification only; this does not count as a new substantive work.
No present acreage, membership, legal entitlement or current program outcome is asserted. No Santee Dakota community review or endorsement is recorded.

profiles.name: Blackfoot

remainingGaps: This is a brief Confederacy route with one selected Siksika publication; substantial Kainai, Piikani and Aamskapi Pikuni community histories and authors remain to be reviewed.

The 2000 declaration itself and original Canadian and United States treaties were not examined; no current legal, boundary or membership conclusion follows from the Council's summary.
No Blackfoot community review or endorsement is recorded. The photograph shows one dated Montana conservation activity, not the entire Confederacy.
